about: pass 2 elements: the pass 1 elements (unchanged) plus the candidates declared in notes-C2.md, pass 2

elements.statement: Members call the room's own members, and kindred subs, to come and place for a work: to start it, build it, finish it or hold it.
elements.range: from one unanswered post asking who will help to a run of calls, cheering and a set time for placing together

elements.statement: The room settles what its mark will show of it: a member proposes a picture, the room argues its design, signs it or leaves it unsigned, or claims a mark others made.
elements.range: from a single member's unanswered proposal to a design argued over days and redone

elements.statement: Members build the mark and report its state, and the state of the canvas itself tells the next placer what is missing: progress, extension, personal pieces on a shared mark.
elements.range: from one report that the logo is half done to a mark grown into several pieces over two days

elements.statement: Members circulate a template or coordinates that fix the output pixel by pixel, ask for them, and hold strays to them.
elements.range: from one anchor coordinate to an official template enforced against versions

elements.statement: Members keep the placed work against erosion: they watch it, repair changed pixels, rally to defend it under attack, cover the night, harden its shape and put upkeep before growth.
elements.range: from one member fixing stray pixels to shifts, scripts and calls to defend over many hours

elements.statement: Members work out who changed their work and why: they trace placers and rooms, find friendly fire or their own mistake, blame officers, or disown placers acting in their name.
elements.range: from one question who keeps adding a line to a dossier on a rival's bots

elements.statement: Rooms spare their neighbours' work without a written agreement, rein in their own attackers, apologise for damage and appeal to attackers to stop.
elements.range: from one member refusing to cover a neighbour to a room restoring a work it had damaged

elements.statement: Rooms settle borders, truces and deals with neighbours by talk, through envoys, hold each other to them and dispute them.
elements.range: from a one-line border agreed in a thread to treaties across languages kept and broken over a day

elements.statement: Rooms attack others' work by the recurring moves the canvas affords: erasing, encroaching, converting a sign, raiding on a streamer's call, planting a script, griefing for fun.
elements.range: from one member's call to deface a rival to a coordinated raid

elements.statement: After the work is erased or overrun, the room weighs fighting for the spot against moving, and moves: a new spot, a smaller version, a fresh start.
elements.range: from a lone member asking where to rebuild to a room relocating together within two hours

elements.statement: When a work is up, the room marks it: announces it, celebrates it, credits makers and helpers, reports members' own parts and says what working with strangers meant.
elements.range: from one 'We did it!' post to threads of credit and reflection at the close

elements.statement: The room records what happened to its work: screenshots and timelapses, reports of its fate, mourning, imagined art, atlas entries, the end marked.
elements.range: from one screenshot request to a full account of the week

elements.statement: At the close the room decides what of its temporary effort to keep: a later canvas, a new purpose for its canvas sub, the mark in its banner, ties with other rooms, the work remade elsewhere.
elements.range: from a wish to do better next year to a canvas-born collective carried into a lasting group

elements.statement: Members multiply their hands beyond the rate limit with scripts, bots and extra accounts, and the room governs these machine hands.
elements.range: from one member running spare accounts to a shared bot holding several rooms' works

elements.statement: A member answers a call or proposal in one line that joins, assents, reports a part done or thanks, and the line asks for nothing back.
elements.range: from 'On it.' to 'Did my part.'

elements.statement: The host sub is keyed as play for April Fools: fakes, takeovers and the one-day licence fill the room, and every claim in it, a call to the canvas included, may be a joke.
elements.range: from one fake post in an ordinary sub to a sub given over to parody for a day and a half

elements.statement: The room judges that it has too few hands or too little room for the work it wants: doubt, a canvas judged too full, a work judged absent or outclassed.
elements.range: from one member saying there are not enough people to defenders told to give up

elements.statement: Rooms aligned their placers mostly without deciding how they were organized: a decided element of order (a leader, a vote, an oath, a sanction, a division of the work) appears in few rooms, and the question who is in charge is almost never asked.
elements.range: from rooms that say they wing it to canvas-born factions holding elections

elements.statement: The starter: a member who proposes the mark, maps it or begins placing it, and whom others then join.
elements.range: from a member who only asks to a member who maps and places alone first

elements.statement: The envoy: a member who acts for a room toward another room, carrying a proposal between threads or chats.
elements.range: from a member calling themself a diplomat once to a standing representative in a shared council

elements.statement: Rooms help one another's works and trade help: they give pixels to a neighbour's mark, ask other rooms for help, barter help for space or repair, thank their allies, greet them, and turn requests away.
elements.range: from one member placing a pixel on a neighbour's flag to rooms trading night-time repairs for room on their mark

elements.statement: Rooms join other rooms in coalitions and host them: they meet in shared chats, form alliances, gather kindred rooms, make joint marks, ask a host for space or vet others' requests to build on their own mark.
elements.range: from two rooms agreeing to defend each other to a flag hosting dozens of other rooms' works by vote

elements.statement: Rooms carry a contest with a rival room in talk: they trade taunts, flood the rival's threads, claim victory, salute the rival after the fight and blame attackers after the close.
elements.range: from one taunt in a thread to days of chants, victory claims and an after-the-fight salute

elements.statement: The community carries a quarrel from before the canvas into it: a rival sub, a sports or national rivalry, an old dispute.
elements.range: from one member naming the sub's old rival to a room whose first canvas act is against that rival
